issues.text: For ORCH and the owner (decisions/0102 item 19). Forms that cannot be refused without refusing an AC0.3 sample of the plan: (a) a value that is a path, `token: data.token` (so `password=hunter.fake` cannot be told from it); (b) a template `${token}` in the Bearer position (a real secret written exactly as `${…}` is not a secret); (c) three dotted parts without the eyJ start, `a.b.c`, `"1.2.3"`, `vendor.min.js` (JWT without eyJ is not found; M7); (d) the 40-character identifier (M10); (e) the line `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` (the body of a certificate is not looked at). All five are the only plan-seed exceptions in the description and are named there as residual risk. Beyond the seeds I also store four classes that decisions/0102 item 14 and the task wording («expression/identifier/call/member access/template placeholder») call non-literal but that no sample demands: a call (`secret: getSecret()`), a bare identifier of the narrow class В3 (type words, names with `_`, camelCase: `token: string`, `password: SecretString`, `Authorization: authHeader`), a shell substitution `$(…)` and a block opener (`token: {`). A secret written exactly in these shapes (`password=correct_horse`, `password=getit(`) is stored, because the old rule hid it and the new one does not. The question to the owner: keep these classes (cost of refusing them measured below), or tighten to path + template only? My proposal: keep as written; refusing them adds +1 file of 1072 in the development dependencies and +35 of 1164 in a large TypeScript client tree (TypeScript types and calls), and does not close the gap of (a).

Cost of the closed refuse set, measured on my sketch of the written rules (not the final code): 2 of 154 own files (tools/src, tools/README.md, docs/*.md at the top level) - both are texts that mention the PEM header (`-----BEGIN`); 27 of 1072 text files of the development dependencies (README badge URLs with `?token=…`, bundled parsers with `this.token=t`, one declaration file); 35 of 684 files of tools/test and docs (baits and quoted examples, expected); 150 of 1164 files of a large TypeScript web client tree on this machine (118 of them by form Ф9: test fixtures such as `token: 'tok'`, `password: 'pw'` - the quoted value is a literal and the closed placeholder list does not contain `tok` or `pw`). A refused file fails the whole attempt without retry. Decision 0102 item 18 keeps the placeholder list closed and says ORCH cannot widen it; whether the owner wants more test words (for example `tok`, `pw`, `fake`) is the owner's decision (option B of the earlier question; item 16 of the record). Until then the cost is named in the description, criterion 11 (README and record) and here.

For ORCH: Addition 4 of decisions/0102 withdrew item 15, but the text of item 15 and the older wording of item 14 («every form … for a literal value») still stand in the record file; the text of REQ-102 now follows item 18 and 20 and refuses more than item 15 accepted: PEM labels other than the certificate (PUBLIC KEY, CERTIFICATE REQUEST, …), the bare `-----BEGIN`, unquoted values under 8 characters or without a digit, quoted values with a space or non-ASCII, a URL password equal to the user name (`app:app@db`; the sample `имя:имя@h` moved from «stored» to «refused»), the 8-character minimum of Bearer/Authorization. Criterion 11(b) requires the record of the code step to say so; the existing file is not mine to edit.

For REQ-VALIDATOR and the test steps: criterion 7 changed shape on purpose (F6): the control of the instrument is one family, k = 1, sizes 8/32/128 KiB and a two-step ratio of at least 64, instead of three families with both ratios at least 8; reasons: the cost (a call of the old control was about 9.4 s at 256 KiB) and the measured first-step ratio of about 10, too close to 8. The separation holds: 140-170 against about 16 for a linear function. The families (1), (6), (8), (9) changed because the new definitions make their old texts secrets; every family was run on the sketch (secret-free at 256 KiB, 1 MiB, 4 MiB; bait at the end found).
